title: Garlic
summary: Central Asian allium — global flavor base for 5,000+ years.
origins: Wild garlic (Allium longicuspis) originated in Central Asia; cultivation spread through Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Mediterranean. Ancient Egyptians fed garlic to pyramid laborers; Greeks and Romans used it medicinally and in cuisine.
history: Garlic traveled the Silk Road and Columbian exchange routes until it appeared in nearly every major cuisine. Louis Pasteur documented its antibacterial properties in 1858. Modern research focuses on allicin — the compound released when cloves are crushed.
teaching: Crushing releases allicin — sharp bite. Mince early, cook gently for sweetness.
Green sprout inside clove is bitter but safe — remove for milder flavor.
Roast whole heads at 400°F for 45 min — squeezeable sweet paste.
fun_fact: Crushing garlic releases allicin — that's the sharp bite. Mince early, cook gently for sweetness.
